'''''Viburnum plicatum''''' is a species of flowering plant in the family [[Viburnaceae]] (formerly [[Caprifoliaceae]]), native to mainland China, Korea, Japan, and Taiwan.<ref name=grin>{{GRIN | access-date = 14 January 2018}}</ref> The Latin [[binomial nomenclature|specific epithet]] ''plicatum'' means "pleated", referring to the texture of the leaves.<ref name=RHSLG>{{cite book | last=Harrison |first=Lorraine | title=RHS Latin for Gardeners | year=2012 |publisher=Mitchell Beazley | location=United Kingdom | isbn=978-1845337315 }}</ref> 

==Description==
[[Image:snowball bush flowers.jpg|thumb|left|"Snowball" flowers of a sterile cultivar]]
Growing to {{convert|3|m|ft|0|abbr=on}} tall, it is a [[deciduous]] shrub. The leaves are opposite, {{convert|5|-|10|cm|0|abbr=on}} long and {{convert|3|-|6|cm|0|abbr=on}} broad, simple [[Ovate (botany)|ovate]] to oval, with a serrated margin. 
[[File:Zaden van een Viburnum plicatum. 20-07-2025. (d.j.b).jpg|thumb|255px| Ripening seeds of a ''Viburnum plicatum'']]

Plants from Taiwan are sometimes distinguished as ''Viburnum plicatum'' var. ''formosanum'' Liu & Ou.<ref name=tesri>[[Taiwan Endemic Species Research Institute]]: [http://www.tesri.gov.tw/content/wild/wild_angiosperm_05.asp ''Viburnum plicatum'' var. ''formosanum''] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080101085508/http://www.tesri.gov.tw/content/wild/wild_angiosperm_05.asp |date=January 1, 2008 }}</ref>

===Inflorescences=== 
The flowers are produced in flat [[corymb]]s {{convert|5|-|10|cm|0|abbr=on}} in diameter, comprising a central cluster of fertile yellowish-white flowers {{convert|5|mm|in||abbr=on}} in diameter, surrounded by a ring of showy, sterile flowers {{Convert abbreviated|2-3|cm|4=1}} in diameter, which act as a target guide to pollinating insects. The fruit is an ovoid blue-black [[drupe]] 8–10 mm long.<ref name=rhs>Huxley, A., ed. (1992). ''New RHS Dictionary of Gardening''. Macmillan {{ISBN|0-333-47494-5}}.</ref><ref name=bean4>Bean, W. J. (1980). ''Trees and Shrubs Hardy in the British Isles'' 8th ed., vol. 4. John Murray {{ISBN|0-7195-2428-8}}.</ref>

==Cultivation==
''Viburnum plicatum'' is a popular [[ornamental plant]], both in its native area and other temperate regions. Some of the more popular [[cultivar]]s are selected for having all of their flowers large and sterile with few or no fertile flowers; their flowerheads resemble a snowball, giving them the popular name '''Japanese snowball bush'''. Cultivars of this type include 'Grandiflorum' and 'Rotundifolium'.

===Cultivars===
Cultivars with wild-type flowerhead structure are sometimes described as a separate [[Form (botany)|botanical form]] ''V. plicatum'' f. ''tomentosum''. They include 'Cascade', 'Lanarth' and 'Rowallane'.<ref name=rhs/><ref name=bean4/>
